webster.text: Redundancy of words in speaking or writing; the use of more words to express ideas, than are necessary.

example.quote: and rather than resort to a construction affecting so essentially the whole character of the government, it would perhaps be more rational to consider the expression as a mere pleonasm or inadvertence.
example.cite: James Madison, Report on the Virginia Resolutions (Report of 1800), Jan. 7, 1800
